page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head across the top, with the page number "62" at the top left. No margin notes. Below the text, the catchword "dunt" at the right.

main_text.p: eorum sæuitia: attamen, quantum in ipsis est, & condemnant, & ignis fornaces aperiunt.

Item. Sunt quidam sic addicti suis opinionibus, ut, quantum in ipsis est, ex die noctem faciant: & quia in absurda imaginatione occaluerunt, non credunt alios recte sapere, his tam iniqui ut malint mendacibus obtrectationibus credere: ne quid dicam de his, qui propter malam conscientiam, quod de aliis dicitur, ad se trahunt, & quicquid de quibusdam loquaris, ad se pertinere putant: atque inde, ut fit, nouas confingunt fabulas & tragoedias, contenti suas suspiciones dicere vel scribere. Item. Non est contendendum cum eo qui dat operam, ut quomodocunq; fiat superior, & modo victor habeatur, veras rationes negligit. Iustinus Martyr in Epist. ad Zenam & Serenum [?].
Philosophiam nomine habituq; profitentur quidam, qui nihil præstant dignum hac professione. Iustinus Martyr in 2. Apologia pro Christianis.

Vereratorie [?] instructi persuadendi arte seducunt mentes imperitorum, eosq; captiuos ducunt, deprauantes eloquia Domini: mali enarratores facti eorum quæ bene dicta sunt. Item. page.notes: Small marks in the left margin (a dot and short strokes beside the first lines) are not legible text and are left out. The reading "Vereratorie" in the second-last section is uncertain. The name in the citation after "Zenam &" is printed as "Serennm" and read here as "Serenum". The "2." after "in" in the Apologia citation is hard to make out. The running head is read as "Charact. Iesvitæ" and may be abbreviated differently. The paragraph "Item. Non est" begins mid-line and is kept inside the same paragraph as printed.
